Insights: n‑Norwegian ⇒ smallest N = (n‑1)/p·(p‑1) where p = smallest prime factor of n‑1. For all given n=M+c (M=3^{2025!}), n‑1 is even ⇒ p=2 ⇒ f(M+c)=(M+c‑1)/2.  

Let k=2025!, A=k/2. Then g(c)= (A+⌊A(c‑1)/M⌋)/k, sum =3+S/k with S=∑⌊A(c‑1)/M⌋. Only c=0 gives –1, c=4M gives 4A‑1, others 0 ⇒ S=4A‑2.  

ΣN=5k‑2 ⇒ Σg=5‑2/k = (5k‑2)/k = (5k‑2)/k reduced by 2 ⇒ p+q=3k‑1.  

Answer = (3·2025! − 1) mod 99991. Compute 2025! mod 99991, multiply by 3, subtract 1.

Insights: For n=M+c (M=3^E huge), minimal N≈2M/3 (f(M)=2M/3). For any fixed small c (c≪M), f(M+c)=2M/3+O(1) ⇒ f/M=2/3+ε with ε≪1/2025!. Hence g(c)=⌊2025!·f/M⌋/2025!=2/3. Only c=4M gives N=4M (f=10/3·M) ⇒ g=10/3. Sum=5·2/3+10/3=20/3 ⇒ p+q=23 ⇒ answer 23. Pitfall: assume N=M*d always minimal; for small c N< M works but still yields same g.

Insights: f(n)=min lcm(a,b,c) for a+b+c=n ⇒ f(N)=N·min_{s|N}T(s) where T(s)=min lcm/s. Minimal ratios: 6/11 (s≡11·k), 4/7 (7·k), 16/25 (25·k), 30/47 (47·k), 64/97 (97·k), 110/167 (167·k). Compute M=3^{2025!} mod s (pow). For N=M+c (c even) all N odd. Check divisibility: N₀,N₁ (c=0,4M) ⇒9|N ⇒R=2/3. Others: N₂ divisible by 25⇒R=16/25; N₃ by 47⇒R=30/47; N₄ by 97⇒R=64/97; N₅ by 167⇒R=110/167. Since 2025!·R integer, g(c)=R. Sum =2/3+2/3+16/25+30/47+64/97+110/167 =224414944/57101475. p+q≡41754 (mod 99991).

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) for a+b+c=n ⇒ ratio r=LCM/s. Minimal r=6/11 (s=11k), next 4/7 (s=7k), 16/25 (s=25k), 64/97, 110/167. For N=M+ c, s|N iff s|c+1 (since M≡1 mod s, s coprime 3).  

M=3^{2025!}≡1 (mod any s∤3).  

c=0 ⇒ N=M not divisible by 3 ⇒ only s multiple of 9 works → r=2/3 ⇒ g(0)=2/3.  

c=4M ⇒ N=5M, still r=2/3, floor term adds 4r ⇒ g=10/3.  

For small c, compute c+1 factorization:  

1848374+1=5²·3²·31·53 → smallest s≠5,≠3 is 25 ⇒ r=16/25.  

10162574+1=5²·3²·31²·47 → s=25 ⇒ r=16/25.  

265710644+1=5·3³·97·103·197 → s=97 ⇒ r=64/97.  

44636594+1=5·3·103·167·173 → s=167 ⇒ r=110/167.  

Thus sum =2/3+10/3+2·16/25+64/97+110/167 =2672218/404975.  

p+q=3077193 ⇒ (p+q) mod 99991 = 77463.  

Pitfalls: ensure s coprime 3 (N not divisible by 3), use smallest s|c+1≥6, compute minimal LCM/s for each s (scale primitive triples).

Insights: n‑Norwegian ⇒ need three divisors a,b,c with a+b+c=n. For n=M+ c (M=3^{2025!}), the largest divisor must be M (or N≈M). Minimal N is M·d where d= min_{a+b=c} lcm( a/3^{v₃(a)}, b/3^{v₃(b)} ). For c≪M, d≈1, so f(M+c)= (2/3)M+O(c) ⇒ f/M=2/3+tiny. Since 2025!·tiny<1, floor gives g(c)=2/3. For c=4M, n=5M ⇒ minimal N=4M ⇒ f/M=10/3 ⇒ g=10/3. Sum=5·2/3+10/3=20/3 ⇒ p+q=23. Pitfall: assume N=M always; need check c large (4M) and small‑c case uses f≈2M/3. Answer: 23.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ f(n)=min_{d|n} (n/d)·f(d) ⇒ f(n)/n = min_{e|n, e≥6} f(e)/e. For n=M+ c (c≠0, c≡2 mod 3) divisors are exactly d|c+1 (coprime to 3). Minimal ratio = min_{prime p|c+1, p≥6 or p^k≥6} f(p)/p (or f(p^k)/p^k). Compute f(p) for needed primes: f(5^2)=16, f(31)=20, f(53)=34, f(47)=30, f(97)=64, f(103)=68, f(167)=110, etc. Results: g(0)=2/3, g(4M)=10/3, g(1848374)=16/25, g(10162574)=30/47, g(265710644)=64/97, g(44636594)=110/167. Sum =125561848/19033825 ⇒ p+q=144595673 ⇒ 144595673 mod 99991 = 8687. Pitfalls: ensure c≡2 (mod 3) so n not divisible by 3; use only divisors of c+1 not divisible by 3; 2025! divisible by all small denominators.

Insights: f(N)=N·min_{s|N} (L_min(s)/s), where L_min(s) is minimal LCM of three distinct numbers summing to s. For M=3^K, only s=9·3^t divide M ⇒ ratio 2/3. For N=M+c (c≪M, c≠4M) N≡1 (mod 3), so any divisor s of N must be coprime to 3 ⇒ s|c+1. Compute L_min(s)/s for each divisor of c+1; pick smallest. Results: g(0)=2/3, g(4M)=10/3, g(1848374)=16/25, g(10162574)=30/47, g(265710644)=64/97, g(44636594)=110/167. Sum =125561848/19033825 ⇒ (p+q) mod 99991 = 8687. Pitfall: assume s=9 always; must check divisors of c+1 for non‑multiple‑of‑3 cases.

Insights: f(n)=min_{d|n}(n/d)·f(d) ⇒ f(n)/n = min_{d|n} f(d)/d. For n=M+ c (c≠0, M=3^K, K=2025!), divisors d (≠3) satisfy d|c+1 and M≡1 (mod d) (since φ(d)≤2025). So g(c)=f(d)/d where d is divisor of c+1 giving minimal ratio f(d)/d. Compute f(d)/d for small d via brute; minimal ratios: c=0 →2/3; c=4M →10/3; c=1848374 →16/25 (d=25); c=10162574 →30/47 (d=47); c=265710644 →64/97 (d=97); c=44636594 →110/167 (d=167). Sum =125561848/19033825 ⇒ p+q≡8687 (mod 99991). Pitfalls: ensure d|M+ c (need M≡1 mod d) and d≤2025 so φ(d) divides K.

Insights: f(n)=min LCM(a,b,c) with a+b+c=n ⇒ f(n)/n=min_{s|n} L_min(s)/s, where L_min(s) is minimal LCM for sum s. For M=3^K, M≡1 (mod 11,7,17,…), so only s|M are powers of 3 ⇒ best ratio 2/3 (s=9). For N=M+c (c≡2 mod 3) divisors are s|c+1 (coprime to 3). Compute L_min(s) for needed s: 25→16/25, 47→30/47, 97→64/97, 167→110/167. Thus g(0)=2/3, g(4M)=10/3, g(1848374)=16/25, g(10162574)=30/47, g(265710644)=64/97, g(44636594)=110/167. Sum=125561848/19033825 ⇒ p+q≡8687 (mod 99991). Pitfalls: ensure s|N (use c+1), 2025! divisible by s, floor term zero for small c.
